text: 7. The statutes governing the world’s most prestigious intellectual prize generally forbid the honoring of those who have already shuffled off this mortal coil. However, a bureaucratic oversight in 2011 led to the announcement of Ralph Steinman as a laureate for his discovery of the dendritic cell, only for the committee to discover he had passed away three days prior. Rather than rescind the honor, the committee made a historic exception to their rigid "living only" policy. What is the name of this specific international award?

When 19th-century European explorers encountered the towering curved walls and dry-stone towers of this African site, they hallucinated origins involving the Phoenicians or the Queen of Sheba, refusing to credit the local population. It wasn't until the archaeological work of Randall-MacIver and Gertrude Caton-Thompson that the site was rightfully attributed to the ancestors of the Shona people. These precise, mortar-less structures served as the royal palace for a kingdom that flourished between the 11th and 15th centuries. What is the name of this archaeological complex?
